cards.name: Blue Cash Preferred Card from American Express

currency.name: Reward Dollars
currency.redemption: Cash back is issued as Reward Dollars (1 Reward Dollar = $1). Redeem as a statement credit or for eligible items at Amazon.com checkout (same value as statement credit; card must be linked to the Amazon account, allow up to 72 hours). No minimum redemption amount (official Cash Back Program terms). Reward Dollars cannot be used to pay the Minimum Due. Statement credits usually appear within about 3 days. Reward Dollars do not expire while the account is open and not past due; they are forfeited if the account is cancelled. Bonus-category rewards can take 8-12 weeks to post (view them on the Bonus Rewards Detail page). No transfer partners.

earning.conditions: Supermarkets located in the U.S. (50 states, PR, USVI and other U.S. territories) only. Cap is $6,000 of eligible purchases per calendar year, resets January 1; after the cap the rate is 1%.
earning.notes: Official definition: a supermarket offers a wide variety of food and household products (meat, fresh produce, dairy, canned/packaged goods, household cleaners, pharmacy products, pet supplies). Rewards Program terms: superstores, convenience stores, warehouse clubs, and meal-kit delivery services are not considered supermarkets. Amex rewards-info examples of ELIGIBLE merchants: ALDI, FreshDirect, Gelson's, Hy-Vee, Kings Food Markets, Meijer, ShopRite, Smart & Final, Stop & Shop, Trader Joe's, Vons, Whole Foods, Winn-Dixie. NOT eligible per Amex: specialty stores (bakeries, butchers, cheese shops, fish markets, liquor stores, wine shops), superstores (Target, Walmart), warehouse clubs (BJ's, Costco), convenience stores (7-Eleven), meal-kit services (Blue Apron, Freshly, HelloFresh), and online superstores/big box (Amazon). Amazon Fresh is not named by Amex; because Amazon is listed as an excluded online superstore, Amazon Fresh orders should be assumed NOT to earn 6% (unverified). Instacart and Walmart Neighborhood Market are reported by secondary sources (WalletHub, forums) to sometimes code as supermarkets, but Amex's terms say purchases on online marketplaces with multiple retailers do not earn additional rewards; treat as unverified. Purchases through third-party payment accounts or third-party card readers may not earn the bonus; Apple Pay/Google Pay/Samsung Pay earn the same as the physical card per Amex FAQ.

earning.conditions: Eligible purchases of U.S. streaming subscriptions from Amex's list of select providers; the subscription must be billed directly by the provider. No spending cap.
earning.notes: Official select-provider list at americanexpress.com/rewards-info (retail page, fetched 2026-09-28; no additions or removals reported by Amex or secondary sources as of 2026-10-02), 32 providers: Amazon Music Unlimited, AMC+, Apple Music, Apple TV+, Audible, Britbox, DirecTV Stream, Discovery+, Disney+, ESPN, Fubo TV, HBO Max, Hulu, iHeartRadio, Kindle Unlimited, Luminary, MGM+, MLB.TV, NBA League Pass, Netflix, Pandora, Paramount+, Peacock, Prime Video, Sling TV, SiriusXM Streaming and Satellite, Spotify, Starz, TIDAL Music, YouTube Music Premium, YouTube Premium, YouTube TV. Rewards Program terms: if a subscription is bundled with another product or service or billed by a third party (such as a digital platform, a cable, telecommunications, or internet provider, or a car manufacturer), the purchase may not be eligible. In practice: Netflix billed through Apple/iTunes, Hulu via Spotify, Disney+ via Verizon, channels via Amazon Prime Video Channels, or Roku billing typically do not earn 6%. MGM+, AMC+, BritBox, Discovery+ and Starz were added 2025-01-30 (NerdWallet).

earning.conditions: Purchases at merchants whose primary business is transit. Not restricted to the U.S. in the Rewards Program terms. No spending cap.
earning.notes: Rewards Program terms: transit includes trains, taxicabs, ride share services, ferries, tolls, parking, buses, and subways; airfare, car rental and cruises are not considered transit. The rewards-info travel page adds that trams are not considered transit and that the list is not exhaustive. Uber/Lyft count as ride share (3%). Parking garages, toll authorities (E-ZPass reloads coded as tolls), Amtrak and commuter rail count when coded as transit merchants.

earning.conditions: Eligible purchases of gasoline at gas stations located in the U.S. No spending cap.
earning.notes: Rewards Program terms: superstores, supermarkets and warehouse clubs that sell gasoline are not considered gas stations (so Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's, Walmart, Kroger/Safeway fuel centers earn 1%). Rewards-info definition: a merchant whose primary business is selling gasoline (examples: Gulf, Murphy USA, Murphy Express, Exxon, Mobil, Hess, Shell); not eligible: marina fuel, commercial fuel (jet fuel), and gas stations located within superstores or warehouse clubs. EV charging is NOT mentioned in the official terms (the category is defined as purchases of gasoline); some third-party sites claim EV charging earns 3%, but this is unverified and should not be relied on.

earning.conditions: All other eligible purchases.
earning.notes: Eligible purchases exclude fees, interest, balance transfers, cash advances, travelers checks, prepaid card purchases/reloads, other cash equivalents, gift cards, person-to-person transactions, and any portion of a purchase covered by Reward Dollars at point of sale.

credits.name: $120 Disney Streaming Credit
credits.schedule: Up to $10 per calendar month; resets on the 1st of each month; maximum $120 in statement credits per calendar year per enrolled card account.
credits.howToUse: Enroll in the Benefits section of the online account or app (Basic Card Member or Authorized Account Manager only; up to 24 hours to take effect). Then buy a monthly or annual subscription, including bundle subscriptions, directly on the U.S. websites DisneyPlus.com, Hulu.com or Stream.ESPN.com, or set the enrolled card as the payment method on an existing Disney/Hulu/ESPN account. No minimum purchase amount since 2025-08-01 (a $9.99 Disney+ with ads plan is fully covered; the $10 cap means pricier plans get $10 back). Qualifying purchases can be one or more transactions in the month; Additional Card Member purchases count but the account total is $10/month. An annual subscription earns only one $10 credit in the month of purchase. NOT eligible: subscriptions bought through a third-party device or digital platform (Apple, Roku, Amazon, Google, etc.) unless it redirects to the Disney/Hulu/ESPN site to pay, bundles with cable services, Disney+ via Verizon or other carriers, advertising services, and gift cards. Credit typically posts in a few days but can take up to 8 weeks; account must not be cancelled or past due at fulfillment; credits may be reversed if the purchase is refunded or cancelled. If the card is replaced, confirm enrollment and update the card on file with Disney. Purchases also earn 6% streaming cash back separately.

credits.name: American Express Venue Collection Concessions Statement Credit (10% back, up to $250/yr)
credits.schedule: 10% back as statement credits on qualifying food and beverage concessions purchases at participating Amex Venue Collection stadiums and arenas, up to $250 in total statement credits per calendar year per enrolled card. Offer ends 2026-12-31 unless extended.
credits.howToUse: Add the offer to the card (Amex Offers-style enrollment), then pay for in-venue food and beverage concessions with that enrolled card at a participating venue. Limit one enrolled card per Card Member across all their Amex cards, so a cardholder with several Amex cards must pick one. Not valid on purchases through third parties (resellers, delivery services, intermediaries). Credits normally post within 30 days, up to 90 days. This is a network-wide benefit available on all U.S. consumer and business Amex-issued cards, not a Blue Cash Preferred exclusive, but it is listed in the Blue Cash Preferred benefit terms.

rentalCar.limit: Up to $50,000 per Rental Agreement for damage to or theft of the rental vehicle (actual repair cost, wholesale book value or purchase price, whichever is less), plus reasonable loss-of-use and towing charges within that limit.
rentalCar.duration: Up to 30 consecutive days per rental agreement (no coverage beyond 30 consecutive days from the same rental company even if the agreement is extended or rewritten).
rentalCar.notes: Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company; Benefit Guide 371-396 Rev. 4/19/2024. Must reserve and pay for the entire rental with the card and decline the rental company's collision damage waiver (CDW/LDW). Coverage is secondary to any other valid insurance. Not available for vehicles rented in Australia, Italy, New Zealand, or OFAC-sanctioned countries. Vehicles not covered include cargo/custom vans, vans seating more than 8, cube/box trucks or trucks with GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more, vehicles used for commercial or hire purposes, leased/mini-leased vehicles, antique cars (20+ years old or out of production 10+ years), limousines, off-road vehicles, motorcycles, mopeds, RVs, golf/motorized carts, campers, trailers. No liability coverage. Losses not covered include off-road operation, intoxication/drugs, intentional damage, wear and tear, tires (unless from a covered collision/vandalism/fire), and damage outside the covered territory. Optional paid Premium Car Rental Protection (primary coverage, per-rental flat fee) is available separately.

purchaseProtection.notes: Covers theft or accidental damage of Covered Purchases charged to the card for up to 90 days from purchase; up to $1,000 per Covered Purchase and $50,000 per Eligible Card per calendar year; natural-disaster losses limited to $500 per event. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company; Benefit Guide 316-401 Rev. 4/19/2024. Not covered: items lost or mysteriously disappeared, consumables/perishables, animals and plants, one-of-a-kind items/antiques/art/furs, used items, motorized devices and parts (vehicles, boats, scooters, etc.), rented/leased/borrowed items, items purchased for play like sports equipment, fraud by the beneficiary, normal wear and tear. Notice of claim within 30 days of loss or as soon as reasonably possible; claims online or 1-800-228-6855.

extendedWarranty.notes: Adds up to 1 additional year to Original Manufacturer's Warranties of 5 years or less on Covered Purchases made in the U.S. or its territories; coverage up to the amount charged, max $10,000 per Covered Purchase and $50,000 per Eligible Card per calendar year. No coverage where the manufacturer warranty plus any purchased service contract exceeds 5 years. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company; Benefit Guide 314-399 Rev. 4/19/2024. Exclusions mirror Purchase Protection (motorized devices, consumables, animals/plants, one-of-a-kind items, used items, etc.). Notice of claim within 30 days of loss.

returnProtection.notes: If the merchant will not take back an eligible item within 90 days of purchase, Amex may refund the full purchase price (excluding shipping and handling) up to $300 per item and $1,000 per Card Member account per calendar year (based on purchase date). Item must be charged entirely to the card and purchased in the U.S. or its territories, in working order, not visibly used, defective or damaged. Call 1-800-228-6855 within 90 days of purchase; original receipt and card record of charge due within 30 days of the call; item may need to be shipped to Amex within 30 days (shipping reimbursed). Not eligible: animals/plants, one-of-a-kind items, limited editions, going-out-of-business sale items, consumables/perishables, jewelry, watches, services, custom-built items, CDs/DVDs/tapes, computer software, firmware/console games, maps, books/magazines, used/personal-use health items, formal wear (bridal, gowns, tuxedos), tickets of any kind, motorized vehicles, and more (see guide). Benefit guide file dated 10/09/2023.

cellPhone.conditions: No cell phone protection on this card (not among the 18 listed benefits).

tripDelay.notes: No trip delay insurance on the Blue Cash Preferred.

lostLuggage.notes: No baggage insurance plan on this card.

roadsideAssistance.notes: No roadside assistance benefit; Global Assist Hotline can refer to third-party services at the cardholder's expense when 100+ miles from home.

travelEmergencyAssistance.notes: Global Assist Hotline: 24/7 emergency assistance and coordination (medical and legal referrals, emergency cash wires, missing luggage assistance, pre-trip destination info) when traveling more than 100 miles from home. Coordination is free but any third-party provider costs are the cardholder's responsibility; it is a referral service, not insurance. 1-800-333-AMEX or collect 1-715-343-7977.

perks.name: Amex Offers
perks.details: Merchant-funded statement-credit or bonus-cash-back offers added weekly; enroll each offer on the card in the app or online before purchasing. Availability is per account (targeted).

perks.name: Redeem Reward Dollars at Amazon.com checkout
perks.details: Link the card to Amazon (Shop with Points) and apply Reward Dollars to all or part of eligible Amazon.com orders at the same value as a statement credit. Amex charges the card the full amount and posts a matching credit; the credit may land in a different billing cycle, and the minimum payment must still be paid.

perks.name: American Express Venue Collection
perks.details: Card Member entrances/fast lanes and special ticket access at participating stadiums and arenas; present the card and a valid ticket. Also the 10% concessions credit listed under credits.

perks.name: Amex Presale Tickets and Amex Reserved Tickets
perks.details: Access to presale and reserved tickets for select events (sports, music, more) when paying with an Amex card; sold by third-party ticket sellers, while supplies last, blackout dates and purchase limits apply.

perks.name: Plan It
perks.details: Split purchases of $100 or more into monthly installments for a fixed monthly plan fee (no interest); up to 10 active plans; purchases with foreign transaction fees and fees such as the annual fee are excluded.

perks.name: Send & Split
perks.details: Send money or split purchases via Venmo/PayPal from the Amex App after enrolling and opening an Amex Send account; adding money to the Send account does not earn rewards and is subject to the purchase APR. No fee to send to U.S. recipients.

perks.name: Additional Card Members at no fee
perks.details: Up to 10 active Additional Card Members (age 13+); their purchases earn Reward Dollars for the basic account. Additional Card Member benefit coverage may vary. Optional spending limits can be set per Additional Card.

perks.name: Instant Card Number
perks.details: If eligible at approval, use the card number online and in Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, PayPal and Amazon Pay before the physical card arrives (full credit line may not be available until the physical card is confirmed).

perks.name: Lowest Hotel Rates Guarantee (Amex Travel)
perks.details: If a qualifying hotel rate booked on amextravel.com or the Amex Travel app is found lower online for the same room/dates/terms, Amex refunds the difference (claims before check-in for prepaid, within 30 days after stay for pay-later; many rate types excluded).

perks.name: Premium Car Rental Protection (optional, paid)
perks.details: Opt-in primary rental coverage for a flat fee per rental period (reported at $12.95-$24.95 depending on plan, up to 42 consecutive days) charged automatically when a rental is paid with the card after enrollment. Listed among the card's 18 benefits; fee amounts taken from Upgraded Points, not verified against the official product page.

perks.name: FICO Score and Insights; CreditSecure (paid); Dispute Resolution; Digital Wallets; Year-End Summary
perks.details: Standard Amex account tools listed on the benefits dashboard. CreditSecure is a paid credit-monitoring add-on.

perks.name: Welcome offer (new accounts, as of 2026-09)
perks.details: Public offer is 'as high as' $300 back after $3,000 in purchases in the first 6 months (amount can be lower depending on applicant); targeted/E*Trade-Morgan Stanley versions have offered $400. Amex once-per-lifetime rule applies, and having had the Morgan Stanley Blue Cash Preferred disqualifies the welcome offer.

cards.acceptance: American Express network. Accepted at the large majority of U.S. merchants, but notable holdouts remain: Costco warehouses and Costco.com accept Visa only (Costco is also excluded from the supermarket and gas categories anyway); some small merchants, landlords and utilities decline Amex. International acceptance is narrower than Visa/Mastercard, and with a 2.7% foreign transaction fee this card should not be used abroad. Transit purchases outside the U.S. can earn 3% but still incur the 2.7% fee.
recentChanges: 2025-08-01: 'Disney Bundle credit' renamed 'Disney Streaming Credit' and raised from up to $7/month ($84/yr) to up to $10/month ($120/yr); the previous $9.99 minimum monthly purchase requirement was removed; standalone Disney+, Hulu or ESPN subscriptions now qualify, not just the bundle. Annual fee unchanged at $95 (TPG, Doctor of Credit, AwardWallet, Upgraded Points; official page reflects new terms). Blue Cash Everyday got the same structure at $7/month.

2026 (early): Public welcome offer moved to an 'as high as $300 after $3,000 in 6 months' model, meaning some applicants are offered less; targeted offers of $400 (E*Trade/Morgan Stanley customers) and $300 pre-approved mailers have circulated (Frequent Miler, Doctor of Credit, US Credit Card Guide).

2026-04-15: Doctor of Credit reported Amex surveyed cardholders on possible Blue Cash Preferred redesigns: annual fee rising to $135 or $160, an option for 8% at U.S. supermarkets (still capped at $6,000), and new monthly credits such as $10 Resy, an AI-subscription credit, a cloud-storage credit, and a PetSmart perk. Secondary write-ups of the survey also describe variants that would cap 6% streaming or cut it to 3%. As of 2026-10-02 NO such change has been announced; the card page still shows $0 intro then $95 and 6%/6%/3%/3%/1%.

Current through 2026-12-31: American Express Venue Collection concessions offer (10% back, up to $250 per calendar year, enrollment required, one card per Card Member) is listed in the card's benefit terms with an end date of 12/31/2026; whether it will be renewed for 2027 is unknown.

No change as of 2026-10-02 to the $6,000 calendar-year supermarket cap, the 6% select-streaming list, the $10/month Disney Streaming Credit, the 3% gas/transit definitions, the $95 annual fee, the 2.7% foreign transaction fee, or the protections (benefit guides last revised 4/19/2024; Return Protection guide 10/2023).
gotchas: The 6% supermarket cap is $6,000 of spend per CALENDAR year (about $500/month) and resets January 1; spend above it earns only 1%, so route overflow grocery spend to another card.

Walmart, Target, Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's, Amazon (including Amazon Fresh, unverified), 7-Eleven/convenience stores, drugstores, specialty food/liquor stores and meal-kit services do NOT count as supermarkets.

Gas at warehouse-club and supermarket fuel centers (Costco, Sam's, BJ's, Kroger, Safeway, Walmart) earns 1%, not 3%; only merchants coded as gas stations earn 3%. EV charging is not part of the official gas definition.

Streaming must be billed directly by the provider: subscriptions billed through Apple/iTunes, Google Play, Roku, Amazon Prime Video Channels, Verizon/T-Mobile, or cable/ISP bundles generally do not earn 6% and do not trigger the Disney credit.

The Disney Streaming Credit requires ENROLLMENT first; without it you get nothing. It is a calendar-month credit (unused months are lost), an annual plan yields only one $10 credit, and the card on file with Disney must be updated if the card number changes.
Reward Dollars can be redeemed in any amount but cannot be applied to the Minimum Due, and they are forfeited if the account is closed; bonus-category cash back can take 8-12 weeks to appear.
Transit excludes airfare, car rentals, cruises and trams; a purchase must be at a merchant coded as transit (rideshare, taxi, parking, tolls, rail, bus, ferry, subway).

Purchases made through third-party payment accounts (e.g., PayPal checkout), online marketplaces with multiple retailers, or merchants using third-party mobile card readers may not earn bonus categories; Apple Pay/Google Pay/Samsung Pay tap-to-pay does earn the same as the card.
2.7% foreign transaction fee: do not use abroad. Amex acceptance gaps (Costco in-store, some small merchants).

The annual fee is $0 only in the first year; from year two the $95 fee applies (plus a Plan It plan cannot be used to pay it). Net value depends on using the $120 Disney credit and spending near the $6,000 grocery cap.

Welcome offer is subject to Amex's once-per-lifetime rule per card product, and prior Morgan Stanley Blue Cash Preferred holders are ineligible; Amex also limits cardholders to a maximum of 5 Amex credit cards and 2 approvals per 90 days (Frequent Miler).

cards.name: Chase Freedom Unlimited

currency.name: Ultimate Rewards (marketed as Cash Back; tracked as points, $1 Cash Back = 100 points)
currency.redemption: Per the Rewards Program Agreement (RPA0509, 09/11/2025): when redeemed for cash (statement credit or electronic deposit to an eligible US Chase account), gift cards, or travel through Chase Travel, each point is worth $0.01 (1.5 points per $1 = 1.5% cash back). No minimum to redeem for cash (card page). Pay-with-points at third parties (e.g., Amazon) may be worth less. Points do not expire while the account is open; 30 days to use them after a voluntary closure; forfeited immediately if closed for misuse/fraud/delinquency. NEW since 2026-09-21 (partially verified): Chase says 'Freedom cards' get rotating Points Boost offers on select hotels via Chase Travel worth up to 10% more (about 1.1 cents/point); TPG names Freedom Unlimited explicitly, but CFU's own product page does not yet mention it. On its own, CFU cannot transfer to airline/hotel partners. COMBINING WITH A HOUSEHOLD SAPPHIRE PREFERRED: the agreement allows moving points only to another Chase Ultimate Rewards card 'belonging to you or one member of your household' (Chase defines household member as someone who shares your address; you may link to only one person). Once in the spouse's Sapphire Preferred the points follow CSP rules: 1:1 transfers to Chase's airline/hotel partners (Aer Lingus, Aeroplan, British Airways, Flying Blue, Iberia, JetBlue, Singapore, Southwest, United, Virgin Atlantic, IHG, Marriott, Wyndham) EXCEPT World of Hyatt, which from a Sapphire Preferred is 4:3 (1,000 UR = 750 Hyatt) since 2026-10-01 for all CSP cardmembers (immediately for CSP applications on/after 2026-06-15); Sapphire Reserve keeps Hyatt at 1:1, and Chase Travel at 1 cent base or Points Boost up to 1.5 cents (hotels/economy) and 1.75 cents (premium-cabin flights). The flat 1.25 cents/point Chase Travel rate NO LONGER applies to newly combined points: since 2025-10-26 it survives only for points that were already in a CSP account (earned or combined) by 2025-10-25, on accounts opened/upgraded before 2025-06-23, and only through 2027-10-26; points are consumed first-in-first-out. Points combined into the CSP today get 1 cent / Points Boost / partner transfers.

earning.conditions: None (no cap, no activation). Category defined by merchant category code.
earning.notes: Agreement wording: '3% Cash Back rewards total for each $1 spent on ... dining at restaurants including takeout and eligible delivery services' (1.5% base + 1.5% bonus). Chase Rewards Category FAQ: restaurants are merchants whose primary business is sit-down or eat-in dining, including fast food and fine dining; delivery and takeout services (third-party delivery apps) qualify only if the merchant is coded as a restaurant. NOT included: food/drink merchants located inside larger establishments such as sports stadiums, hotels, casinos, theme parks, grocery stores and department stores; bakeries; caterers; meal-kit delivery services; gift-card merchants. Purchases through third-party payment accounts or digital wallets earn the bonus only if the technology passes the restaurant category. Unlike some Chase cards' 'dining when purchased directly from a restaurant' category, CFU's category does include eligible third-party delivery.

earning.conditions: None (no cap, no activation). Category defined by merchant category code.
earning.notes: Agreement wording: '3% Cash Back rewards total for each $1 spent on purchases in the following rewards categories: drugstores ...'. Chase FAQ: drugstores are merchants that specialize in selling prescription drugs and over-the-counter medicines, supplements and health-related items, and may also sell cosmetics, toiletries and household goods (e.g., stand-alone CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid). NOT included: warehouse clubs, discount stores, grocery stores, or any merchant that sells a wide variety of goods and merely has an onsite pharmacy (e.g., pharmacy counters inside Target, Walmart, Costco, Kroger). Gift cards bought at a drugstore earn 3% only because the merchant is coded as a drugstore; Chase's agreement treats gift-card reselling as misuse.

earning.conditions: Booked and paid with the card through Chase Travel (chasetravel.com or the number on the back of the card). Only the portion paid with the card earns; any portion paid with points earns nothing.
earning.notes: Agreement wording: '5% Cash Back rewards total for each $1 spent on purchases made using your card through Chase Travel' (1.5% base + 3.5%). Chase FAQ: prepaid travel purchases on chasetravel.com or by phone, including airline tickets, hotels, car rentals, cruises, activities and tours. Excluded: bookings through FROSCH by Chase Travel / Valerie Wilson Travel / Frosch International Travel (they do not earn the 5%), and independent travel advisors. Travel booked directly with airlines, hotels, Expedia, etc. earns only 1.5%.

earning.conditions: All purchases not in a bonus category.
earning.notes: Agreement: '1.5% Cash Back rewards for each $1 spent ... equal to 1.5 points'. Not purchases (earn nothing): balance transfers, cash advances, cash-like transactions (travelers checks, foreign currency, money orders, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, lottery/casino/betting, person-to-person transfers, account funding), convenience checks, interest, fees, fraudulent charges. Points post at the close of each billing cycle; returns/refunds are deducted and can produce a negative balance.

merchantRates.conditions: Qualifying Lyft products and services purchased through the Lyft mobile app with the card as the payment method (PayPal/digital wallets in the Lyft app excluded per lyft.com/chase).
merchantRates.notes: Card-page footnote: 'You'll earn 2% cash back total on qualifying Lyft products and services purchased through the Lyft mobile application through 09/30/2027. That's 0.5% additional cash back on top of the 1.5%.' Qualifying: rideshare; bike and scooter rides; subscription and membership products (e.g., Lyft Pink). Excluded: gift cards, car rentals, vehicle service centers, miscellaneous fees. The former 5% Lyft rate ENDED 2025-03-31; 2% has applied since 2025-04-01 (Doctor of Credit 2025-03-31). Lyft is a taxi/rideshare MCC, so without the promo it earns 1.5%.

credits.name: DoorDash $10 off one non-restaurant order per quarter
credits.schedule: One $10 discount per calendar quarter (Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep, Oct-Dec) through 2027-12-31; unused amount is forfeited at quarter end. Available from 2025-02-01.
credits.howToUse: Add the Freedom Unlimited as the default payment method in the DoorDash (or Caviar) app and click the Chase DashPass activation (activation must occur between 2025-02-01 and 2027-12-31, US address required). The $10 is applied as a promo at checkout on one qualifying NON-restaurant order (grocery, convenience, retail, alcohol, etc.) that meets the app's subtotal minimum; it applies to the subtotal only, not fees, taxes or tip. You must remain enrolled in DashPass and pay with the enrolled Chase card itself, not via Apple Pay/Google Pay. Limit one redemption per quarter per person; changing DashPass plan during the promo forfeits the offer. This is a checkout discount, NOT a statement credit.

rentalCar.limit: $60,000 (theft, collision damage, valid loss-of-use, administrative fees, reasonable towing)
rentalCar.duration: Rental periods up to 31 consecutive days
rentalCar.notes: Guide to Benefits (effective 10/1/2024): secondary in the US (pays deductible and what personal auto insurance does not; acts as primary if you have no auto insurance); PRIMARY outside the US where available. Must pay the entire rental with the card and/or Ultimate Rewards and DECLINE the rental company's CDW/LDW (accepting it voids the benefit). Covers the primary renter plus additional drivers on the rental agreement. Not covered: exotic vehicles or MSRP over $125,000; antique cars (over 20 years old or out of production 10+ years); cargo vans; trucks other than pickups; motorcycles/mopeds; limousines and chauffeured vehicles; RVs; passenger vans seating more than 12; peer-to-peer car sharing (e.g., Turo); rentals exceeding or intended to exceed 31 days; leases; liability, injury, personal belongings, diminished value, DUI, off-road. Report within 100 days of the incident (chasecardbenefits.com or 1-800-349-2691); documents within 365 days.

purchaseProtection.notes: Per item $500; $50,000 per account (lifetime of account, not per year, per the guide). Covers theft, damage, and 'involuntary and accidental parting' within 120 days of purchase (90 days for New York residents). Secondary to homeowner's/renter's/other insurance (covers your deductible). Exclusions include: animals/plants, antiques/collectibles, motorized vehicles, software, items for resale or commercial use, items lost or 'mysteriously disappeared', items in a common carrier's care, perishables/consumables, cash/tickets/gift cards, used items. File within 90 days of loss; documents within 120 days. Purchases made partly with points are covered.

extendedWarranty.notes: Adds 1 year to an original manufacturer's US repair warranty of 3 years or less; total coverage never exceeds 4 years from purchase. If a store warranty or purchased service contract exists, coverage starts after those end, and there is NO coverage if the manufacturer warranty plus store warranty plus service contract already exceed 3 years. Limits: $10,000 per item, $50,000 per account. Exclusions: motorized vehicles and accessories, software, medical equipment, rented/leased items, items for resale/commercial use, used items (refurbished with warranty OK). File within 90 days of failure; documents within 120 days. Store receipts/warranties at chasecardbenefits.com.

returnProtection.notes: Not in the Freedom Guide to Benefits.

cellPhone.notes: Freedom Unlimited has never carried cell phone protection (that was a Freedom Flex/Mastercard benefit, and Chase removed it from Freedom Flex effective 2026-09-20).

tripDelay.notes: Not included in the Freedom Guide to Benefits.

tripCancellation.notes: $1,500 per covered traveler and $6,000 per trip for all covered travelers (no separate annual cap stated). Covered travelers: you and your family members (spouse/domestic partner, children, parents, siblings, grandparents, etc. per the guide's definition) even if not traveling with you, when all or part of the trip is charged to the card and/or paid with Ultimate Rewards. Reimburses non-refundable prepaid COMMON CARRIER fares (planes, trains, ferries, cruise ships; not taxis, rideshare, rental cars, commuter rail), carrier change fees, award redeposit fees, and up to $250 ground transport for medical interruptions. Covered reasons: death, accidental injury or illness of traveler/companion/family member (physician-advised), severe weather and named-storm warnings, change in military orders, organized public-transport strike (20% of trip lost), certain terrorist incidents/travel warnings. Not covered: change of plans or financial reasons, pre-existing conditions (60-day lookback), epidemics/pandemics or border closures, carrier insolvency, pregnancy after 26 weeks, trips over 60 days, missing visas/passports. Secondary to other insurance. Notify within 20 days; documents within 90 days.

baggageDelay.notes: Not included in the Freedom Guide to Benefits.

lostLuggage.notes: No lost-luggage reimbursement. The Travel and Emergency Assistance benefit offers only a 'Lost Luggage Locator Service' (help with the carrier's claim); replacement costs are yours.

travelAccident.notes: Not included in the Freedom Guide to Benefits.

roadsideAssistance.notes: PAY-PER-USE 'Roadside Assistance' (Chase marketing calls it Roadside Dispatch): 24/7 in the US and Canada, no enrollment, call 1-800-349-2691. You pay a pre-negotiated per-service fee quoted on the call (fee is not fixed in the guide). Services: standard towing up to 5 miles, tire change (with usable spare), battery jump-start (EVs towed to nearest charger), lockout (no key replacement), fuel delivery up to 5 gallons (fuel cost extra), winching within 100 feet of a paved road. Light-duty vehicles (10,000 lb or less) only; not an insurance benefit; may be discontinued at any time.

travelEmergencyAssistance.notes: 24/7/365 referral and coordination service (1-800-349-2691 US; 001-214-503-2951 collect abroad): emergency message relay, medical and legal referrals, emergency transportation arrangements, ticket replacement help, lost-luggage locator, translation, prescription/document delivery arrangements, pre-trip information. Covers you and immediate family (spouse/domestic partner, dependent children under 26). The cardholder pays ALL actual medical, legal, transport and other costs; this is not insurance. Not available in sanctioned countries or where the State Department has a travel warning.

perks.name: Combine points with a household member's Sapphire Preferred
perks.details: Rewards Program Agreement: 'You can move your points, but only to another Chase card with Ultimate Rewards belonging to you or one member of your household.' Transfers are blocked if either account is currently prohibited from earning/using points. Chase's household page: the household member must share your address (spouse, partner, roommate or family member you live with); you can link with only ONE person; not friends/family at another address. How: chase.com or Chase app > Ultimate Rewards > pick the Freedom Unlimited > Rewards details > 'Combine points' > choose source card (CFU) and destination card (spouse's CSP) > enter amount > Review > Submit; moves are instant and there is no fee. Secondary sources (TPG July 2026; AwardWallet Sept 2026) report that the FIRST time you link another person's account you must call the number on the back of the card so a rep can verify the household relationship and add the CSP account number; after that it appears as a destination online. Chase's own article describes entering the recipient's information online, so the phone step may not always be required. Once combined, the points are the spouse's and follow CSP redemption rules (1:1 partner transfers, except World of Hyatt at 4:3 from a Sapphire Preferred since 2026-10-01; Chase Travel at 1 cent or Points Boost up to 1.5/1.75 cents; the legacy 1.25 cents applies only to points that were in the CSP by 2025-10-25 on pre-2025-06-23 accounts, through 2027-10-26).

perks.name: Complimentary DoorDash DashPass (6 months)
perks.details: 6 months of complimentary DashPass ($0 delivery fees and reduced service fees on eligible DoorDash and Caviar orders) when you activate for the first time between 2025-02-01 and 2027-12-31 with the Freedom Unlimited set as default payment in the DoorDash app. After 6 months you are AUTOMATICALLY ENROLLED and charged the then-current monthly DashPass rate unless you cancel in the DoorDash app. Membership must be activated with a US address; one DashPass benefit per person even with multiple Chase cards; changing plans during the promo forfeits it. Also unlocks the $10 quarterly non-restaurant promo listed under credits.

perks.name: Points Boost on select hotels via Chase Travel (Freedom cards)
perks.details: Chase press release 2026-09-21: 'Chase Freedom cardmembers can now also access rotating Points Boost offers when redeeming points on select hotels booked through Chase Travel, with Ultimate Rewards points worth up to 10% more' (i.e., up to about 1.1 cents/point; hotels only, no flights). The release body is about Freedom Flex, but its footnote says 'up to 10% more for Freedom cards depending on the offer', and The Points Guy (updated 2026-09-21) states Chase expanded Points Boost to Freedom Unlimited, Freedom Flex and the original Freedom. Marked unverified because the Freedom Unlimited product page and the 09/11/2025 program agreement do not mention it yet. Boosted hotels show a rocket icon in Chase Travel. Chase's education page 'Chase Ultimate Rewards: How Our Program Works' (seen via search index 2026-10-02) also says Freedom Unlimited cardmembers may be able to use Points Boost on select bookings; still unconfirmed on the CFU product page/agreement.

perks.name: Chase Offers
perks.details: Targeted merchant cash-back offers you activate in the Chase app or on chase.com; posts as a statement credit after a qualifying purchase (offer-specific caps and expirations).

perks.name: Chase Pay Over Time (My Chase Plan)
perks.details: Split eligible purchases into fixed monthly payments (3-24 months) for a fixed monthly fee instead of interest; interest-free intro period applies to new accounts (0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 15 months, then 18.24%-27.74% variable per pricing & terms as of 12/16/2025).

perks.name: Chase Credit Journey
perks.details: Free credit score, Experian-provided score plans and identity monitoring; available to anyone but surfaced as a card feature.

perks.name: Zero Liability and 24/7 fraud monitoring
perks.details: Standard Chase/Visa zero-liability for unauthorized charges; fraud alerts by text/email/phone.

perks.name: New-cardmember bonus (current standard offer)
perks.details: $200 (awarded as 20,000 points) after $500 in purchases in the first 3 months from account opening; not available to current cardmembers or anyone who received a CFU bonus in the last 24 months. Limited-time bumps have appeared ($300 through 2026-01-15; $250 during 2026-03-16 to 2026-04-30; in-branch $200 plus 5% on gas and grocery for the first year in May 2026).

cards.acceptance: Visa (issued as Visa Platinum or Visa Signature depending on credit line; both carry the same Freedom Guide to Benefits). Costco: US warehouses and Costco gas stations accept 'All Visa Cards' (Mastercard is NOT accepted in-warehouse but is on Costco.com), so the CFU works at Costco in-store at 1.5% (warehouse clubs are excluded from the drugstore category). Visa is accepted essentially everywhere in the US and worldwide, but every non-USD or foreign-merchant transaction incurs the 3% foreign transaction fee, so it is a poor card for use abroad (unlike Freedom Flex, which dropped its FTF on 2026-09-21).
recentChanges: 2025-06-23 / 2025-10-26: Chase 'Points Boost' replaced the fixed 1.25 cents (Sapphire Preferred) and 1.5 cents (Sapphire Reserve) Chase Travel rates. Legacy rates survive only for points already in those accounts by 2025-10-25 (accounts opened/upgraded before 2025-06-23), through 2027-10-26. Points combined from a Freedom Unlimited into a Sapphire Preferred on or after 2025-10-26 get 1 cent or Points Boost (up to 1.5/1.75 cents), not 1.25 cents. Partner transfers unchanged at 1:1.
2025-09-11: Rewards Program Agreement revised (RPA0509). Earning structure unchanged (1.5% / 3% dining and drugstores / 5% Chase Travel); FROSCH bookings explicitly excluded from 5%.
2026-01-15: Limited-time $300 (30,000-point) welcome bonus ended; standard offer reverted to $200 after $500 in 3 months (Frequent Miler 2026-01-08).
2026-03-16 to 2026-04-30: Limited-time $250 welcome bonus after $500 spend (NerdWallet; seen only via search summary, not fetched).
2026-05: In-branch-only offer: $200 after $500 plus 5% back on gas and grocery for the first year (Doctor of Credit 2026-05-07; Frequent Miler).

2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31: TARGETED promo (email) for existing cardholders: 3% back on either gas stations or grocery stores, up to $1,500 in spend, activation required by 2026-09-15 (Doctor of Credit 2026-08-11). Not a public benefit.

2026-09-21: Chase refreshed the sibling Freedom Flex (no foreign transaction fee, hotel Points Boost up to 10% more, $250 bonus, cell phone protection removed 2026-09-20). Chase's release says Points Boost hotel offers now reach 'Freedom cards' generally and TPG names Freedom Unlimited; however Freedom Unlimited KEEPS its 3% foreign transaction fee (Doctor of Credit 2026-09-22: 'The Freedom Unlimited still has a foreign transaction fee'; CFU pricing & terms still show 3%). Freedom Unlimited only received new card art at the same time (Doctor of Credit); no CFU earning/fee changes. Watch for a CFU refresh.

2026-10-01: Chase Sapphire Preferred (and Ink Business Preferred) transfers to World of Hyatt dropped from 1:1 to 4:3 for cardmembers who applied before 2026-06-15 (already 4:3 for applications on/after 2026-06-15); Sapphire Reserve keeps 1:1. Freedom Unlimited points combined into a household CSP now get 750 Hyatt points per 1,000 (about a 25% cut for Hyatt redemptions); other partners unchanged at 1:1 (chase.com Sapphire Preferred benefits page; Chase newsroom 'Meet the New Chase Sapphire Preferred').
Announced/scheduled: Lyft 2% runs through 2027-09-30; DoorDash DashPass activation and $10 quarterly promo run through 2027-12-31; legacy 1.25-cent CSP redemption window closes 2027-10-26.
gotchas: Lyft is 2% total, not 5%. The 5% Lyft rate ended 2025-03-31 (2% since 2025-04-01, through 2027-09-30). Card must be the payment method inside the Lyft app; PayPal/wallet payments and gift cards do not qualify.

3% dining depends on the merchant's code: restaurants inside hotels, casinos, stadiums, theme parks, grocery and department stores, plus bakeries, caterers and meal-kit services, often earn only 1.5%. Third-party delivery apps count only when coded as restaurants (they usually are); check the statement's bonus line.
3% drugstores means stand-alone drugstores. Pharmacy counters inside Target, Walmart, Costco, Kroger, etc. earn 1.5% because those merchants are coded as discount/grocery/warehouse.

5% travel requires booking THROUGH Chase Travel and paying with the card; direct airline/hotel bookings earn 1.5%. Any portion paid with points earns nothing, and FROSCH/Valerie Wilson advisor bookings are excluded. Chase Travel bookings are often less flexible than direct bookings and may forfeit elite credit/benefits.

The DoorDash $10 quarterly benefit is a checkout promo on NON-restaurant orders (grocery, convenience, retail) only, requires active DashPass, must be paid with the physical card credential (not Apple/Google Pay), and is forfeited if unused by quarter end. DashPass auto-renews at the paid rate after the 6 free months.

There is currently no Instacart benefit on this card even though many 2024 articles still describe one (the Freedom Instacart+ / $10 quarterly benefit ended 2024-07-31; Chase's 2025-2027 Instacart program covers co-brand and Ink cards only).
3% foreign transaction fee: do not use abroad or with foreign online merchants; Freedom Flex (since 2026-09-21) and Sapphire cards have no FTF.

Points are worth a flat 1 cent on the CFU itself. To get transfer partners or Points Boost you must combine into a Sapphire/Ink Preferred; a household member's card qualifies only if they share your address, you may link with only one person, and the first link typically requires a phone call.

Combining into a spouse's Sapphire Preferred TODAY does not unlock 1.25 cents in Chase Travel: that legacy rate applies only to points that were already in the CSP by 2025-10-25 (on pre-2025-06-23 accounts) and expires 2027-10-26. Newly combined points redeem at 1 cent, Points Boost (up to 1.5/1.75 cents on select bookings), or partner transfers (1:1, except World of Hyatt at 4:3 from a Sapphire Preferred since 2026-10-01).

Purchase protection is $500 per item (lower than Sapphire's $10,000) and is secondary to homeowner's/renter's insurance; extended warranty only applies when the total of manufacturer + store + service-contract warranties is 3 years or less.

Rental car coverage is SECONDARY in the US (your own auto policy pays first; the card covers your deductible) and excludes Turo-style peer-to-peer rentals, trucks other than pickups, and vehicles over $125,000 MSRP.
No trip delay, baggage delay, lost luggage reimbursement, travel accident or cell phone insurance. Roadside 'assistance' is pay-per-use, not a free tow.
Sign-up bonus eligibility: not available if you currently hold the card or received a CFU bonus in the past 24 months; Chase's 5/24 rule generally applies to approval.
Chase considers manufactured spending, buying/selling points, and reselling gift cards bought with points to be misuse and can freeze or forfeit points.

cards.name: Prime Visa

currency.name: Amazon Rewards % back (tracked as points; 100 points = $1)
currency.redemption: Rewards are '% back' tracked as points: each $1 of % back = 100 points, and each point is worth $0.01 for every headline redemption option (Rewards Program Agreement RPA0441_0510 dated 01/09/2026). Options: (1) Shop with Points at Amazon.com checkout for all or part of an eligible order, no minimum, points usable 'as soon as the next day' because Daily Rewards post Sunday-Friday; also in-store at Whole Foods Market via the In-Store Code in the Amazon Shopping or Whole Foods Market app (not for Whole Foods pickup/delivery; in-store coffee/juice/liquor bars and eateries may not accept it); also at Amazon SWP properties and participating Amazon Pay merchants. (2) Cash back as a statement credit or electronic deposit to an eligible US Chase account at chase.com/amazon. (3) Gift cards through chase.com/amazon (Amazon help says minimum redemption amounts apply to gift cards and cash back at Chase.com; CNBC reports gift cards in $25 increments; exact cash minimum not verified). (4) Travel booked through Chase Travel (chasetravel.com or phone; phone booking may carry a service fee) at 1 cent per point. Points are NOT Ultimate Rewards: they cannot be transferred to airline/hotel partners or pooled/combined with other Chase cards. Points do not expire while the account is open; if the account is closed for reasons other than misuse/fraud you get at least 30 days to use them; closure for misuse, fraud, bankruptcy risk, or failure to comply with Chase agreements forfeits all points immediately. Portions of a purchase paid with points do not earn rewards. Returns are deducted and can create a negative balance.

earning.conditions: Requires an eligible Prime membership on the Amazon.com account the card is loaded into, with this card confirmed/selected as the 5% card in Manage Payment Options. Only one card per Prime account earns 5%. Without eligible Prime the same purchases earn 3%.
earning.notes: Chase/Amazon definition (Offer Details + RPA 01/09/2026): eligible purchases at Amazon.com 'including digital downloads, Amazon.com Gift Cards, Amazon Fresh orders, Amazon Prime subscriptions, and items sold by third-party merchants through Amazon.com's marketplace'. Amazon's benefits page (amazon.com/primevisa/benefits, Sept 2026) adds: Prime Video, Kindle Unlimited purchases, Amazon Pharmacy, One Medical, PillPack, Amazon Fresh (online or in-store), and purchases at Twitch and Woot using Amazon Pay; Audible.com and Shopbop.com/app are listed as participating Amazon sites. EXCLUDED from 5%: merchants using Amazon Pay other than Twitch/Woot; international Amazon sites (Amazon.ca, .co.uk, .de, .fr, .co.jp, etc.); Zappos, Ring, AbeBooks, Blink, Eero, Amazon Games, Wondery, Amazon Music, and Buy with Prime; any other Amazon-operated site not listed. Purchases on which you choose Amazon promotional financing / equal monthly payments earn NO rewards. Portions paid with gift-card balance or points do not earn. Amazon Business (business.amazon.com) is not listed as participating or excluded on the official page; treat as unverified. Eligible Prime = annual/monthly Prime, Amazon Household members (excluding Prime Video-only subscriptions and invited guests), Prime Fresh, Amazon Family, Prime Student, and Prime trials; only US Amazon.com accounts.

earning.conditions: Eligible Prime membership required (3% without).
earning.notes: Any physical Whole Foods Market in the US, wholefoodsmarket.com, and Whole Foods orders placed on Amazon.com/the Amazon app (delivery/pickup). In-store purchases paid with the Amazon app In-Store Code with Prime Visa selected count as Whole Foods purchases. 'This benefit is in addition to any in-store promotions.' EXCLUDED: international Whole Foods; Whole Foods products bought through third-party sites such as Eventbrite, Instacart, Google Express and Shipt; online Whole Foods gift cards (incl. buyatab.com), event tickets or classes; certain third-party vendors operating inside stores; massage services; Spa@Ink.

earning.conditions: Eligible Prime membership required (3% without). Must book through Chase Travel (chasetravel.com or the number on the back of the card).
earning.notes: Prepaid travel booked through Chase Travel: airline tickets, hotels, car rentals, cruises. Not earned on bookings through FROSCH/Valerie Wilson by Chase Travel, nor on purchases made directly with airlines, hotels, car rental companies or cruise lines. Only the portion paid with the card (not points) earns.

earning.conditions: None (earned with or without Prime). Unlimited.
earning.notes: Chase definition: 'Merchants in this category sell automotive gasoline that can be paid for either at the pump or inside the station, and may or may not sell other goods or services at their location.' Excludes merchants that do not specialize in automotive gasoline: truck stops, boat marinas, oil and propane distributors, home heating companies. EV charging is a separate Chase category not offered on this card; standalone EV charging networks do not earn 2%. Merchant-code based: superstore/warehouse-club fuel pumps earn 2% only if coded as gas stations (Chase does not guarantee coding).

earning.conditions: None (earned with or without Prime). Unlimited.
earning.notes: Chase definition: merchants whose 'primary business is sit-down or eat-in dining, including fast food restaurants and fine dining establishments'; 'Delivery and takeout services will be included if they classify as a restaurant merchant.' Excludes food/drink merchants inside sports stadiums, hotels and casinos, theme parks, grocery and department stores unless coded as restaurants; excludes bakeries, caterers, meal kit delivery services, and gift card merchants. Food-delivery apps (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub) generally code as restaurants but Chase does not guarantee it.

earning.conditions: None (earned with or without Prime). Unlimited.
earning.notes: Chase 'local transit and commuting' definition: 'operators of passenger trains, buses, taxis, limousines, rideshare, ferries, toll bridges and highways, and parking lots and garages.' Excludes 'airlines, hotels, car rental agencies, cruise lines, travel agencies, discount travel sites, vacation clubs, tour operators, bike or scooter rentals and car sharing.' Long-distance/commuter trains earn if coded as passenger rail. Purchases via third-party payment accounts or digital wallets not set up to pass the merchant category will not qualify.

earning.conditions: None. Part of the 'local transit and commuting (including rideshare)' category.
earning.notes: Issuer names 'rideshare' generically; Uber and Lyft are not named individually. Uber Eats / food delivery is not rideshare (see dining). Car sharing (e.g., Turo, Zipcar) and bike/scooter rentals are excluded.

earning.conditions: None. Unlimited.
earning.notes: Excluded from earning entirely: balance transfers, cash advances, cash-like transactions (money orders, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, gambling, P2P transfers, account funding), checks that access the account, interest, fees, unauthorized charges, and Amazon purchases placed on promotional financing/equal monthly payments.

merchantRates.notes: Listed as a participating Amazon site on amazon.com/primevisa/benefits and in Chase's 5% headline since roughly July 2026 (Wayback: 'Amazon Fresh' wording through 2026-06-08 snapshot; 'Audible.com' wording from 2026-07-12 snapshot).

merchantRates.conditions: Eligible Prime membership (3% without); excludes Shopbop gift cards
merchantRates.notes: Listed as a participating Amazon site on amazon.com/primevisa/benefits.
Explicit exception to the Amazon Pay exclusion on amazon.com/primevisa/benefits.
Explicit exception to the Amazon Pay exclusion on amazon.com/primevisa/benefits and Amazon help.
